notes.text: Behold — The prophet having given one eminent instance of God's certain fore-knowledge, in the deliverance of the Jews by Cyrus, now adds another more eminent example of it, by foretelling the coming of the Messiah. This place therefore is expressly interpreted of Christ, Matt. xii, 18, &c. And to him, and to him only, all the particulars following, truly and evidently belong. Whom - Whom I will enable to do and suffer all those things which belong to his office. Elect - Chosen by me to this great work. Delighteth - Both for himself and for all his people, being fully satisfied with that sacrifice, which he shall offer up to me. Bring forth - Shall publish or shew, as this word is translated, Matt. xii, 18. Judgment - The law, and will, and counsel of God, concerning man's salvation. Gentiles - Not only to the Jews, but to the Heathen nations.
Cry — In a way of contention, or ostentation. Lift - His voice. Heard - As contentious and vain-glorious persons frequently do.

Break — Christ will not deal rigorously with those that come to him, but he will use all gentleness, cherishing the smallest beginnings of grace, comforting and healing wounded consciences. Quench - That wick of a candle which is almost extinct, he will not quench, but revive and kindle it again. Judgment - The law of God, or the doctrine of the gospel, which he will bring forth, unto, with, or according to truth, that is, truly and faithfully.
'Till — 'Till he has established his law or doctrine, among the nations of the earth. Isles - The countries remote from Judea, shall gladly receive his doctrine.
He — This description of God's infinite power, is seasonably added, to give them assurance of the certain accomplishment of his promises.

Called thee — To declare my righteousness, or faithfulness. With-hold - Will give thee counsel and strength for the work. Give thee - To be the mediator in whom my covenant of grace is confirmed with mankind. The people - Of all people, not only of Jews but Gentiles. A light - To enlighten them with true and saving knowledge.

The Lord — Hebrew. Jehovah: who have all being in and of myself, and give being to all my creatures. The everlasting, and unchangeable, and omnipotent God, who therefore both can, and will fulfil all my promises.
I tell you — That when they come to pass, you may know that I am God, and that this is my work.

glossa.text:
*Behold my servant.* ((HIER.)) It is to be noted that the apostles are called Jacob, Israel, and the seed of Abraham, to whom afterward, as to servants and men, it is said: *Fear not, worm of Jacob,* etc. But Christ is called not the seed of Jacob or of Israel, but the servant.

*I have given my Spirit.* In the conception; whence: *The Holy Spirit shall come upon thee,* etc. ((Phil. II)). And it shone forth in the baptism, when the Spirit in the likeness of a dove rested upon him ((Luc. I)).

*Smoking flax.* The priesthood now almost extinguished; and of flax is the priestly vestment made.

*He shall bring forth judgment.* He shall judge, namely, not fearing the Scribes and the Pharisees.

*He shall not be sad.* ((ID.)) This Matthew did not set down; or else the words between the one *judgment* and the other were taken away by a copyist's error. And the sense is: he shall preserve at all times an evenness of countenance; which the philosophers falsely boast of Socrates, namely that he was neither sadder nor gladder than his wont.

*Judgment in the earth.* Whence: *For judgment I came into this world, that they who do not see may see,* etc. ((Joan. IX)).
*Justice.* It was just that he who was despised by the Jews should pass over through the apostles to the Gentiles.
*The bound.* With the cords of sins: in the Gospel, the Lord loosed him whom Satan had bound.
*To another.* The Son and the Holy Spirit is not another than the Father in the Godhead, and therefore has the same glory and the same praise.

*I will make known to you.* That you may know that I am the Lord, and there is none other beside me: and that you who behold the former things fulfilled may believe the things to come which I promise.

notes.text: Ye — Ye potentates and rulers of the earth. Glory - By an humble and thankful acknowledgment of it.
Give, &c. — The honour which he deserves: own him as the Almighty, and the only true God. Holiness - Or, in his holy and beautiful house.

The waters — Above in the clouds, which are called waters, Gen. i, 7 chap. xviii, 11. The Divine power displays itself in those high places, which are far above the reach of all earthly potentates. Many - Upon the clouds, in which there are vast treasures of water, and upon which God is said to sit or ride, chap. xviii, 10, 11; civ, 3.
Lebanon — A place famous for strong and lofty cedars.

Them — The cedars; which being broken by the thunder, the parts of them are suddenly and violently hurled hither and thither. Sirion - An high mountain beyond Jordan joining to Lebanon. Lebanon and Sirion are said to skip or leap, both here, and chap. cxiv, 4, by a poetical hyperbole.
The flames — The lightnings.
Kadesh — An eminent wilderness, vast and terrible, and well known to the Israelites, and wherein possibly they had seen, and observed some such effects of thunder.

To calve — Through the terror it causes, which hastens the birth. He names the hinds, because they bring forth their young with difficulty, Job xxxix, 1, 2. Discovereth - Hebrew. maketh bare, of its trees, which it breaks or strips of their leaves. Glory - Having shewed the terrible effects of God's power in other places, he now shews the blessed privilege of God's people, that are praising God in his temple, when the rest of the world are trembling under the tokens of his displeasure.

The flood — The most violent waters, which sometimes fall from the clouds upon the earth. These are fitly mentioned, as being many times the companions of great thunders. And this may be alleged as another reason, why God's people praised him in his temple, because as he sends terrible tempests and thunders, so he also restrains and over-rules them. Sitteth - He doth sit, and will sit as king forever, sending such tempests when it pleaseth him. He praises God for delivering him, and exhorts others to praise him, ver. 1-5. Recollects his former security, and his prayer when in trouble, ver. 6-10. And stirs himself up to thankfulness, ver. 11, 12. A Psalm and song, at the dedication of the house of David. Title of the psalm. Song - A psalm to be sung with the voice to an instrument. David - At the dedication of David's house, which was built, 2 Sam. v, 11, and doubtless was dedicated, as God had commanded.

glossa.text:
*A psalm of David in the consummation.* ((ID.)) The ark brought back from the Philistines, etc., *as far as* that they may offer themselves to such a consummator.

*Bring to the Lord.* ((ID.)) First he admonishes that sacrifices be offered.

 *The sons of rams.* ((AUG.)) Because assault is not wanting, etc., *as far as* and the seventy-two disciples sent to preach are signified.

*The voice of the Lord.* ((CASS.)) The preaching of Christ terrified minds within, which is, that it gave the spirit of fear to the Jews and to the Gentiles.

((GREG.)) This man ascends from the lowest, that is, from the spirit of fear to the spirit of wisdom, etc., *as far as* that is, spiritual understanding: these the Lord shakes.

((HIER.)) As a husbandman a barren land, etc., *as far as* and he will give strength, and will bless the same in eternal peace.

*The voice of the Lord upon the waters,* etc. ((CASS.)) Of the establishing of the Church, where he enumerates the powers of the Holy Ghost with great proclamation.

*Of Libanus.* Libanus is interpreted a whitening. *The cedars of Libanus,* that is, high men lifted up in earthly things, whom God by breaking will crush small, that is, will bring them back from pride to himself through his beloved Son: and this he will crush by the spirit of fortitude, as a unicorn taken is crushed.
*The desert.* ((CASS., AUG.)) The Jewish people, etc., *as far as* whence flows the living water.

*The Lord.* He shews what is done for the Church now established.

*I have given,* he says, *you power to tread down upon serpents.* But as it is unheard of that stags should strike every kind of wild beast with the horn; so that the Apostles, unlettered, should refute all philosophy.

 *A flood.* ((CASS.)) The waters of baptism, which purges the crimes of the world.

notes.text: I perceive of a truth — More clearly than ever, from such a concurrence of circumstances. That God is not a respecter of persons - Is not partial in his love. The words mean, in a particular sense, that he does not confine his love to one nation; in a general, that he is loving to every man, and willeth all men should be saved.

But in every nation he that feareth God and worketh righteousness — He that, first, reverences God, as great, wise, good, the cause, end, and governor of all things; and secondly, from this awful regard to him, not only avoids all known evil, but endeavours, according to the best light he has, to do all things well; is accepted of him - Through Christ, though he knows him not. The assertion is express, and admits of no exception. He is in the favour of God, whether enjoying his written word and ordinances or not. Nevertheless the addition of these is an unspeakable blessing to those who were before in some measure accepted. Otherwise God would never have sent an angel from heaven to direct Cornelius to St. Peter.

This is the word which God sent — When he sent his Son into the world, preaching - Proclaiming by him-peace between God and man, whether Jew or Gentile, by the God-man. He is Lord of both; yea, Lord of and over all.

Ye know the word which was published — You know the facts in general, the meaning of which I shall now more particularly explain and confirm to you. The baptism which John preached - To which he invited them by his preaching, in token of their repentance. This began in Galilee, which is near Cesarea.

How God anointed Jesus — Particularly at his baptism, thereby inaugurating him to his office: with the Holy Ghost and with power - It is worthy our remark, that frequently when the Holy Ghost is mentioned there is added a word particularly adapted to the present circumstance. So the deacons were to be full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom, chap. vi, 3. Barnabas was full of the Holy Ghost and faith, chap. xi, 24. The disciples were filled with joy, and with the Holy Ghost, chap. xiii, 52. And here, where his mighty works are mentioned, Christ himself is said to be anointed with the Holy Ghost and with power. For God was with him-He speaks sparingly here of the majesty of Christ, as considering the state of his hearers.
Not now to all the people — As before his death; to us who did eat and drink with him - That is, conversed familiarly and continually with him, in the time of his ministry.

It is he who is ordained by God the Judge of the living and the dead — Of all men, whether they are alive at his coming, or had died before it. This was declaring to them, in the strongest terms, how entirely their happiness depended on a timely and humble subjection to him who was to be their final Judge.

To him give all the prophets witness — Speaking to heathens he does not quote any in particular; that every one who believeth in him - Whether he be Jew or Gentile; receiveth remission of sins - Though he had not before either feared God, or worked righteousness.

glossa.text: *He is not a respecter of persons,* etc. ((BEDA.)) It is plain that God is not a respecter of persons, etc., *as far as* but that they should receive all that believe.

*You know,* etc. ((RAB.)) It is to be read thus: You know Jesus as John preached him: Jesus of Nazareth, how he anointed him, etc. Or: this John preached, that he anointed him, not indeed after an earthly manner, but by the spirit and the power of signs.

*Who went about,* etc. In the Greek is added, *through forty days,* not that they ate and drank with him daily, for it would be contrary to John, who interposes eight days in which he was not seen by them, that he might be made manifest the third time, and for as many days he fasted before his death, being in need of food, whereas he ate after the resurrection being now not in need of food. He fasted before his death, that we might abstain from the desires of this world. He ate, teaching by this that he is with us until the consummation of the world. Fasting is in the contest, because he who is in the struggle abstains from all things. Food is in the hope of peace, which shall be perfect, when this mortal shall have put on immortality. But we, while we take the way of the Lord, fast from the vanity of the world, and are refreshed by the promise to come.

((RAB.)) Through forty days, not continually, but at certain turns taken within that quadragenary number of days.

*And we drank. ((BEDA.))* Here Peter sets forth what is passed over in silence in the Gospel, that after the resurrection he drank with Christ, unless perhaps we believe it to be indicated there, where he says: *Until I drink it with you in the kingdom of my Father ((Matth. XXVI))*.

notes.text: Mark i, 9; Luke iii, 21

It becometh us to fulfil all righteousness — It becometh every messenger of God to observe all his righteous ordinances. But the particular meaning of our Lord seems to be, that it becometh us to do (me to receive baptism, and you to administer it) in order to fulfil, that is, that I may fully perform every part of the righteous law of God, and the commission he hath given me.

And Jesus being baptized — Let our Lord's submitting to baptism teach us a holy exactness in the observance of those institutions which owe their obligation merely to a Divine command. Surely thus it becometh all his followers to fulfil all righteousness. Jesus had no sin to wash away. And yet he was baptized. And God owned his ordinance, so as to make it the season of pouring forth the Holy Spirit upon him. And where can we expect this sacred effusion, but in an humble attendance on Divine appointments? Lo, the heavens were opened, and he saw the Spirit of God - St. Luke adds, in a bodily form - Probably in a glorious appearance of fire, perhaps in the shape of a dove, descending with a hovering motion, till it rested upon him. This was a visible token of those secret operations of the blessed Spirit, by which he was anointed in a peculiar manner; and abundantly fitted for his public work.

And lo, a voice — We have here a glorious manifestation of the ever - blessed Trinity: the Father speaking from heaven, the Son spoken to, the Holy Ghost descending upon him. In whom I delight - What an encomium is this! How poor to this are all other kinds of praise! To be the pleasure, the delight of God, this is praise indeed: this is true glory: this is the highest, the brightest light, that virtue can appear in.

glossa.text: *Then he came.* When John was preaching and baptizing, namely when Jesus was thirty years old, showing that no one ought to be made a priest or a preacher save at a serviceable age. As Joseph at thirty took up the rule of Egypt. David began his reign at that age: Ezekiel merited the gift of prophecy. Jesus came for these causes, that he might approve the baptism of John, and that (because he was man) he might fulfil all righteousness and the humility of the law: and that, sanctifying the waters, he might show through the dove the coming of the Holy Spirit in the laver. For he came not out of any need of washing, but that no one, however holy, should judge the grace of baptism superfluous. *From Galilee to the Jordan.* Galilee, a passing over: the Jordan, a going down. He therefore who wishes to be baptized, let him pass over from vices, and going down, let him be humbled.

*Suffer it now.* Suffer me now to be baptized by thee, that afterwards thou mayest be baptized in the Spirit with that which thou seekest of me. For as it is fitting to give an example of fulfilling all righteousness, that all may learn that no one is perfect without the water of baptism.

*Then he suffered him.* When he had come to know that righteousness was to be fulfilled in such an order. He suffered him, because that is true humility which its companion obedience does not desert.

The Spirit taught him in a moment what he had not known before, and therefore what he had before humbly feared, he devoutly fulfilled.

*And being baptized.* Christ sanctified the waters of baptism: because it belongs to him whose it is to create, to sanctify also.

As man consists of two things, that is, of body and of soul, so he is reborn of two: of water, which cleanses filth and buries him together with Christ: and of the fire of the Spirit, by whose blaze we are caught up to heaven. So the Church after baptism reaches after the summit of the virtues by certain increases, as Christ when baptized came up out of the water. So after baptism those go up who advance to the virtues: and those who before were carnal and sons of Adam become spiritual and sons of God.

*They were opened,* etc. And this too belongs to the fulfilling of righteousness. For not then for the first time did the heavenly things lie open to him, nor was the Holy Spirit then given: but he showed that to us, through the baptism we have received, the entrance of heaven lies open, and that the Holy Spirit is given. For that the heavens were opened, that the Holy Spirit came, that the voice of the Father sounded, etc., these mystical things are within us.

The entrance into heaven lies open to the reborn through Christ, which through Adam had been closed.

*As a dove.* He had a true body, formed for the hour, in the appearance of a dove: because otherwise the Spirit could not be seen by men as a dove, not because it was a true dove, but because the Spirit was in a bodily appearance, yet was not itself a body. So of this figure it is judged as of the others in which God appeared: which, their office fulfilled, were dissolved. Fitly the Spirit came down in a dove, which is simple and gentle, that he might point out both the simplicity of his own nature, and him upon whom he was descending, the meek herald and giver of mercy. In like manner all who are reborn by baptism ought to be filled with the seven virtues signified in the dove. The dove is a stranger to the malice of gall, in which we are forbidden anger. It wounds none with beak or claws, in which innocence is marked. Nor does it fall upon the smallest little birds, on which other birds feed themselves and their young: in which we are forbidden robbery. It feeds on clean grain: in which abstinence is marked, it cherishes the young of others as its own, behold charity. It gives a moan for a song, behold compunction. It sits above the waters, that by the shadow foreseen in the waters it may turn aside from the hawk: behold watchfulness. In a dove the Spirit appeared above the Lord: because he came to gather us through meekness. Above the disciples in fire, whom he was coming to kindle against their own selves for the consuming of the rust of sin. Adam by sinning lost heaven, Christ appeared glorified by the Holy Spirit through the dove: the quivering flame which barred the way, the water of baptism quenched: because water is contrary to fire.

*I am well pleased.* That is, I have established my good pleasure, that thou, in whom is nothing but good, mayest please, and that through thee others may please, not in themselves, but in thee, that is, united to thee by faith and brightness.

registers.label: Spare
lines: The voice of the Lord is over the waters.
The God of glory thunders.
Jesus comes to the river and goes down into the water.
The heavens open over him.
The Spirit descends like a dove, and a voice speaks.
This is my beloved.
Come, let us worship at the water's edge.
You are my beloved. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Stand with him at the river's edge, the cold water moving over the stones, and watch him wade out and go under.
You are my beloved.
The sky tears open above the water, and the Spirit comes down soft as a dove, and a voice rolls across the river.
You are my beloved.
This is the same voice the prophet heard — calling a servant by name, gentle enough not to break a bruised reed.
You are my beloved.
And the voice is not only for him; it is spoken over every one of you the waters have claimed.
You are my beloved. Thanks be to God!
